name: Fathom Mage
oracle_text:
Evolve (Whenever a creature you control enters, if that creature has greater power or toughness than this creature, put a +1/+1 counter on this creature.)
Whenever a +1/+1 counter is put on this creature, you may draw a card.
blocked_sentences: Whenever a +1/+1 counter is put on this creature, you may draw a card.
scope: ONLY the second line is blocked, and only by one word of it: the counter KIND. The `counter_placed` trigger exists and fires, `source: "self"` narrows it to this permanent, and `may` + `draw` say the rest -- but nothing anywhere can say *which kind* of counter, so the closest expressible card reads 'whenever ANY counter is put on this creature, you may draw a card'. The evolve line is fully expressible today and was verified end to end (see `expressible_today`). The card goes here rather than being written three-quarters because the approximation is a real card advantage engine that is silently wrong, and because it is the draw trigger, not evolve, that anyone plays Fathom Mage for.

needs.what: A way for a `counter_placed` trigger to name the counter kind it cares about -- e.g. `{"event": "counter_placed", "source": "self", "counter": "+1/+1"}` -- so it fires on +1/+1 counters and stays silent on charge, slumber, quest or -1/-1 counters. The data is already on the event and merely never read: `primitives.add_counters` (`engine/primitives.py:234-242`) fires COUNTER_PLACED with `counter=kind` in `event.data`. Three small edits close it: add `counter: str | None = None` to `TriggerModel` (`cards/schema.py:50-67`) and `TriggerSpec` (`engine/carddef.py:95-110`), carry it through `loader._compile_ability` (`cards/loader.py:369-377`) with the same guard the neighbouring `defending` and `not_cause` fields get -- reject it on any event other than `counter_placed`, because a filter that silently never applies is exactly the defect this is fixing -- and check it in `triggers._matches` (`engine/triggers.py:182-226`) as `if spec.counter is not None and event.data.get("counter") != spec.counter: return False`. Worth also adding `"counter"` to the keys `triggers._queue` copies out of `event.data` into `bindings` (`engine/triggers.py:385-387`, which already copies `amount`), so an effect can read the kind that fired it. Note the printed wording is 'a +1/+1 counter', singular-or-more: `add_counters` fires ONE event for the whole batch (`amount` is on the event), so one trigger per placement is already the correct Magic behaviour for both this card and Sharktocrab's 'one or more' phrasing -- no batching work is needed.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: There is no field for it and no selector that reaches it, and both near misses were probed rather than assumed. (1) `{"counter": "+1/+1"}` on the trigger itself is rejected at load: `TriggerModel` is `model_config = Strict` = `ConfigDict(extra="forbid")` (`cards/schema.py:15,53`), verified -> `abilities.0.trigger.counter: Extra inputs are not permitted`. (2) `{"counter": "+1/+1"}` inside the trigger's `filter` is rejected too, verified -> `abilities[0].trigger.filter: unknown selector keys ['counter']`, and it could not work anyway: `matches_card_filter` (`engine/triggers.py:275-332`) matches the SUBJECT OBJECT's printed card face -- types, subtypes, colors, keywords, power, toughness -- and for `counter_placed` the subject is the permanent that received the counter, i.e. this creature. It has no access to the event payload at all. (3) The trigger's `condition` cannot rescue it either: `evaluate_condition` is called from `triggers._matches:220-224` with only `controller` and `source`, so it can ask about the board but never about the event, and `_queue` does not copy `counter` into `bindings` (`engine/triggers.py:385-387` copies `amount`, `damage`, `life`, `sid`, `defender`, `was_attacking` -- not `counter`), so the effects cannot read the kind on resolution either. A `counters_on` self check in an `if` is a different sentence, not a workaround: it is true whenever the creature already has a +1/+1 counter from any earlier source, so a slumber counter arriving later would still draw. The bare unfiltered trigger was built and run: with `{"event": "counter_placed", "source": "self"}` and nothing else, placing a `charge` counter and placing a `slumber` counter each queued the draw trigger just as a `+1/+1` counter did. Those kinds are not hypothetical -- `data/cards/` already places `charge` (4 sites) and `slumber` (4 sites) counters today, so the approximation is observably wrong in the shipped pool, not just in principle. No card in `data/cards/` currently uses `counter_placed` at all, so nothing shipped is approximated yet; Sharktocrab's gap record (`data/authoring/gaps/sharktocrab.json`) carries the same sentence as expressible, which it is not -- whoever clears `adapt` there will hit this.

expressible_today.note: The evolve line needs NO new vocabulary. Recorded in full, verified in a real game, so whoever adds the counter-kind filter can write the whole card in one pass. This is the same shape `data/authoring/gaps/gyre_sage.json` recorded and verified for the identical evolve line; re-run here against Fathom Mage's own 1/1 body.

ability.text: Evolve (Whenever a creature you control enters, if that creature has greater power or toughness than this creature, put a +1/+1 counter on this creature.)

the_second_ability_once_unblocked.text: Whenever a +1/+1 counter is put on this creature, you may draw a card.

expressible_today.why_it_works: `permanent_enters` binds the entering object's oid as `subject` (`engine/triggers.py:382-384`) and `stack.py` builds the resolving ability's `EffectContext` with those bindings, so the effects CAN read it; `values._characteristic` accepts both `{"binding": "subject"}` and `{"self": true}` and reads DERIVED characteristics, so the comparison sees counters already on Fathom Mage and grows past 1, 2, 3 correctly. The comparison must live in the effects, NOT in the trigger's `condition` -- gyre_sage's record documents that trap in full: the condition slot loads cleanly and makes the ability permanently inert, because `evaluate_condition` builds a context with empty bindings and `{"binding": "subject"}` resolves to nothing. `exclude_self` is on the filter because evolve is 'whenever a creature you control enters' meaning another one; without it the ability inspects itself on its own arrival, where the comparison is 1 > 1 and false, so it is harmless either way -- but stating it is what the printed card means. Verified in a real game, not just at load: Fathom Mage on the battlefield with a Simic mana base, Acidic Slime (2/2) cast from hand, all triggers resolved -> Fathom Mage at `{'+1/+1': 1}` and one card drawn, i.e. the evolve counter correctly chained into the draw trigger. That chain is the point of the card and it already works; only the kind filter is missing.
expressible_today.expectation_if_the_card_were_written: `{"zone": "battlefield", "battlefield_count": 33}` -- in the verification sandbox nothing enters after the card under test, so evolve cannot fire, no counter is ever placed, and both a `counters` and a `hand_size`/`library_size` assertion would be dishonest.
